title: The Priest Comes as a Sinner

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is how Aaron is to enter the Most Holy Place: He must first bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. He is to put on the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body; he is to tie the linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are sacred garments; so he must bathe himself with water before he puts them on." - Lev 16:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what Aaron brings first — a sin offering for himself.

The high priest of Israel, the holiest office in the nation, could not walk into God's presence on his own account. Before he could represent anyone else, he had to deal with his own sin. He bathes. He changes. He brings a bull.

And notice the clothes. On this one day he does not wear the magnificent garments described in Exodus — the gold, the jewels, the breastpiece. He wears plain linen, the dress of a servant. On the day he goes furthest into God's presence, he goes lowest in appearance.

Hebrews draws out both details. Our high priest is unlike Aaron in that He does not need to offer sacrifices for his own sins (Heb 7:27). Jesus had none to offer for.

But the humbling is exactly what He did do. He who was in very nature God... made himself nothing by taking the very nature of a servant (Phil 2:6-7). Aaron dressed as a servant for a day. Christ became one.

Every human priest had to start by admitting he needed the altar himself. Only one Priest ever walked in clean.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever help others spiritually while avoiding your own need?
2. What does Christ's humility say to your ambitions?
3. Where might God be calling you to serve in plain clothes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You needed no offering for Yourself and yet took the place of a servant for me. Keep me humble, and let me never forget my own need of grace. Amen.
